rules.statement: After V stopped the woman stalking Blue Moon, V told Blue Moon the stalker should be left for the police ("Maybe we'd better leave it to the badges"), and she was not killed at that decision.
When it came to deciding the captured stalker's fate, V killed the woman who had been stalking Blue Moon, in front of Blue Moon, instead of leaving her for the police.

Backstage at Riot, the confrontation between Kerry Eurodyne and Us Cracks over the label's scheme ended in reconciliation: Kerry accepted the band and Blue Moon answered that there were no hard feelings.
Backstage at Riot, Kerry Eurodyne and V pressured Us Cracks until Blue Moon agreed to cancel the show; the confrontation ended in coercion rather than reconciliation.
Answering Lizzy Wizzy's call, V came to her room at the No-Tell Motel and found Liam Northom dead there with her.
After the chase in Sinnerman, V agreed to go with Joshua Stephenson ("All right. I'll go with you") while Rachel Casich, his producer, was there urging them to move.
After the chase in Sinnerman, V turned on Joshua Stephenson in front of Rachel Casich and the quest recorded him as neutralized; this alone does not establish whether he died.
At PieZ, Rachel Casich offered V money to walk away from Joshua Stephenson, and V took the deal.
At PieZ, Rachel Casich offered V money to walk away from Joshua Stephenson, and V refused ("My answer's no").
In Rachel Casich's braindance studio, V agreed to do it and personally drove the nails during Joshua Stephenson's recorded crucifixion.
In Rachel Casich's braindance studio, V refused to nail Joshua Stephenson but stayed at his side until he died while the crucifixion was recorded.
When the crucifixion recording was about to start, V refused to take part in or even watch it and walked out of Rachel Casich's braindance studio.
Jim Jarry texted V an invitation to race again on his circuit; V replied turning him down ("not lookin to lose my license").
Jim Jarry texted V an invitation to race on his circuit and V accepted ("You had me at burnt rubber"); Jim replied he would see V on the track.
At the agents' final meeting for Spy in the Jungle, V left Bana's biomonitor with Ana Friedman rather than destroying it, with Steven Santos present.
At the agents' final meeting for Spy in the Jungle, V sided with Steven Santos ("Steven's right. Too much risk") and destroyed Bana's biomonitor in front of Ana Friedman.
Following Steven Santos's urgent message not to give it to Ana Friedman, V left Bana's biomonitor at the fixer's drop point, the route Steven asked for so the evidence would be destroyed.

Taking charge of Shank's BD shoot, V settled Lina and Tool's fight by telling Tool he was Lina's sister, so the shoot went ahead as a sister act; this was a performance framing, not a real family tie.
Taking charge of Shank's BD shoot, V convinced Tool he was a clone created by the FIA to get the scene made; it was a cover story, not Tool's real origin.
Taking charge of Shank's BD shoot, V handed Tool his own letter as his "lines", the route meant to shock him out of his Lina persona.
After Dazed and Confused, Rachel Casich messaged V that Lina and Toolina had pitched her their "Lina&Toolina" show and asked whether V knew them.
After Dazed and Confused, Rachel Casich messaged V about Lina and TooLina with open contempt; this version is sent only when her earlier Passion production with Joshua had flopped.
During V's AV flight to Lizzie's Bar on the Corpo path, V took an unscheduled holocall from their Quantified Satori life coach about troubling biometric readings.
The MaxTac data breach left Chang Hoon Nam struggling to find words; when he handed V the convoy data, V told him he had to leave Night City.
V brought Iris Tanner to Dakota Smith without Iris's car; the optional objective to retrieve the car was marked failed (left behind or wrecked).
